unit.title: Numbers to 1000
unit.blurb: Reading, writing and making 3-digit numbers, comparing and ordering them, and rounding to the nearest 10 and 100.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Understand the value of each digit in a 3-digit number: hundreds, tens and ones.

O2.t: Compare and order numbers up to 1000 using the symbols <, > and =.

O3.t: Estimate and round 3-digit numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

p: A 3-digit number has **hundreds**, **tens** and **ones**. In **472** there are 4 hundreds, 7 tens and 2 ones.
We only use ten digits, 0 to 9. The place of a digit tells us its size: each place to the left is worth 10 times more.
So the 3 in 300 is worth 10 times the 3 in 30.

lesson.t: Find the value of a digit
p: Say which place the digit is in: hundreds, tens or ones.
Hundreds: multiply by 100. Tens: multiply by 10. Ones: it stays the same.

p: To compare, look at the **hundreds** first. If they are the same, look at the **tens**, then the **ones**.
**<** means 'is less than' and **>** means 'is greater than': 345 < 354.

lesson.t: Why we start with the biggest place
p: A hundred is bigger than any number of tens, so the hundreds digit decides first.
Only when the hundreds are the same do we look at the tens, then the ones.

steps: the tens and ones do not matter now

p: Line the numbers up by place value.
Compare the hundreds. If they are the same, compare the tens, then the ones.
Write < or >. The open side faces the bigger number.

lesson.t: The mouth eats the bigger number
p: The open side of < or > always faces the bigger number.

p: To round to the nearest **10**, look at the **ones** digit. 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 rounds down. 347 → **350**.
To round to the nearest **100**, look at the **tens** digit. 347 → **300**.

lesson.t: Why we look at the next digit
p: Rounding finds the nearest ten or hundred. The digit to the right tells us which one is nearer.
5 is exactly halfway, so we agree to round up.

steps: 465 is between 460 and 470; the ones digit is 5
465 is between 400 and 500; the tens digit is 6

p: Find the two tens (or hundreds) the number is between.
Look at the digit just to the right.
0–4: round down. 5–9: round up.
45 is exactly halfway between 40 and 50. We round it up to 50.
